f.title: Classify seriousness using the SAHPRA criteria and medical judgement
f.statement: A serious adverse event or reaction is any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose results in death, is life-threatening (patient at risk of death at the time of the event), requires hospitalisation or prolongs existing hospitalisation, results in a congenital anomaly/birth defect, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, or is a medically significant/important event. Medical and scientific judgement should be exercised to decide whether other situations are serious, such as events that may jeopardise the patient or require intervention to prevent one of the listed outcomes (e.g. blood dyscrasias or convulsions not resulting in hospitalisation, development of drug dependency or abuse).
